findings: Volume-preserving advection work gives force -c*grad(mu), equivalent modulo pressure to mu*grad(c). For the given quadratic free energy the projected force is -GRADIENT*lap(c)*grad(c), matching the oracle sign.

The reference uses cell chemical potential, forward cell-to-face gradient G, and backward divergence -G*. Its Fourier pressure projection I-G*G*/|G|² enforces staggered incompressibility and removes the mean velocity.
Face-averaged composition is shared by reversible force and conservative advection, making their work identity exact on the discrete grid. Stokes projection gives nonnegative viscous dissipation.

Single Fourier stripes have chemical potential proportional to composition, so the force is a pure gradient and calibration decay is exact for both closures. Unequal wave magnitudes yield the missing solenoidal capillary force.
